sections.content: Force Powers are extraordinary abilities wielded by Force-sensitive individuals, drawing upon the mystical energy field that binds the galaxy. These powers are learned and developed over time, often requiring significant dedication and training. All Force powers are presented as tiered abilities, allowing for progressive mastery and increasing effectiveness. The GM may waive FP/EP costs for trivial, narrative uses of a power outside combat; powers with listed costs — rituals especially — always pay them when the stakes are real. Any use still requires a successful associated skill roll.

content: **Initial FP:** Your starting Force Points are equal to your Will score.

**Gaining FP:** Force Points come back with time, rest and meditation. A Force-sensitive character recovers 1 FP per hour of light activity -- travel, conversation, ordinary work. Undisturbed rest restores an eighth of maximum FP per hour (round down, minimum 1), and 8 hours of rest restore FP to full whatever the rounding. Meditation is fastest: a character who succeeds at a Meditation roll (Chapter 3) enters a trance and recovers 1 FP for every 3 minutes it is kept up uninterrupted; on a failure, the time counts as rest. No FP returns during a turn in which the character spends FP or maintains a power. A full night’s sleep (8 hours) restores FP to full; a missed or short night restores it only in part, at the Gamemaster’s call.

**Maximum FP:** Your maximum Force Point pool is equal to your Will score. This limit can be permanently increased by purchasing the Force Training advantage or by spending Character Points directly. Another way your maximum FP can increase is via a lightsaber crystal (Chapter 12's Adegan color table: a flat +1, or a multiplier of x1.25, x1.5 or x2). Apply flat bonuses first, then the multiplier, and drop all fractions in the final value.

**Using a Power:** Using a power is your maneuver for the turn; no power in this chapter is used on another character’s turn. Force Barrier, for one, is raised on your own turn and kept up at its per-turn cost.

**A Crystal's FP Bonus Needs Attunement, Not Ignition:** The bonus applies while the character carries the lightsaber, whether it is stowed, readied, or lit -- a kyber crystal is attuned to its wielder, and that bond does not switch off when the blade does. It is lost only if the weapon is lost, destroyed, or given away. Where a crystal's effect is meant to require an active blade the entry says so explicitly (Stygium's +4 to Stealth applies “when ignited”); an effect with no such wording is always on. Only one crystal's FP modifier applies at a time -- the best one the character carries. A wielder with two lightsabers, or a saberstaff with a crystal in each end, does not multiply them together.
**When Maximum FP Changes:** Changing your maximum changes the ceiling, never the pool.

**Gaining maximum FP gives headroom, not points.** Attuning a new crystal, buying Force Training or spending CP leaves your current FP unchanged; it climbs toward the new maximum by the ordinary recovery rules.

**Losing maximum FP clamps you down to it.** If your current FP now exceeds the new maximum it drops to that maximum immediately and the difference is gone. A character with Will 20 and a ×1.5 crystal has a maximum of 30; sitting at 28 when the crystal is lost, they drop to their new maximum of 20.
**A saber is not a battery.** Attuning one before a fight and dropping it afterward never nets a single Force Point.

**The clamp only moves current downward, and never past 0.** Current FP is never raised to meet a rising maximum, and never raised off a negative total by a falling one -- a character at -6 FP in Force Exhaustion who loses a crystal is still at -6, because -6 does not exceed any maximum. Losing maximum FP therefore cannot by itself push a character into Force Exhaustion or deepen it.
**FP Loss:** Using Force Powers consumes FP as indicated in their respective tables. If a Force Power’s FP cost reduces your current FP to 0 or less, you suffer from Force Exhaustion.

sections.content: **At 0 FP or below:** you can still activate Force Powers, but each attempt requires a Will roll. Failure means the power fizzles — its FP cost still applies, driving you further negative — and the strain bleeds over into physical fatigue: you take 1d-3 (minimum 1) EP damage.

**For every point below 0 FP:** you take a continuous −1 to both DX and Will, tracking your current FP total — not a one-time hit, it shrinks automatically as FP recovers. If either attribute drops to 0, you lose consciousness.

**Recovery:** follows the same rules as FP itself (Gaining FP, above) — 1 FP per hour of light activity, an eighth of maximum FP per hour of rest, 1 per 3 minutes of meditation, or a full restore after a full night's rest. There is no separate healing track to manage; the DX/Will penalty simply fades as FP climbs back toward 0.

Alignment measures the character, not the connection. The GM tracks a Force Alignment for every character on a numerical scale from -100 (Pure Dark Side) to +100 (Pure Light Side), Force-sensitive or not, droid or organic. What differs is what that number does. Everyone is subject to the universal effects below -- a cruel mercenary is exactly as hard to govern as a cruel Sith, because self-mastery is a matter of character. The Force-specific effects that follow them (cost, availability, discord, corruption) apply only to characters who can actually touch the Force: it is the Force that turns character into capability, which is why a fallen Jedi is dangerous in a way a fallen smuggler is not.

content: **Gaining Alignment Points**
**Light Side (LS) Points:** Acts of compassion, selflessness, self-sacrifice, defense of the innocent, healing, and seeking knowledge for the greater good typically grant LS points.
**Dark Side (DS) Points:** Acts of aggression, hatred, fear, vengeance, selfishness, manipulation, causing harm for personal gain, and seeking power for its own sake typically grant DS points.

**Universal Effects (Everyone):** The following apply to every character with an Alignment, Force-sensitive or not. Unlike the Force-specific modifiers below, they are read off two thresholds rather than computed per point -- the scale stays one number the GM tracks, with legible cliffs instead of arithmetic on every roll. Aligned is |Alignment| 25 or more; Deeply Aligned is 75 or more.

**Self-Mastery:** The Dark Side's price is the ability to govern yourself. Apply the following to every self-control roll (Chapter 5: Berserk, Cowardice, Charitable, Gluttony and the rest), and equally to any Will roll made to resist fear, temptation, coercion or torture: -1 at Dark 25 or deeper, -2 at Dark 75 or deeper, +1 at Light 25 or deeper, +2 at Light 75 or deeper. The mirror is exact in both directions and on both kinds of roll -- a character who has given themselves over to fear and anger is by that fact easier to frighten and easier to tempt, which is how most of them fell in the first place. This is the one effect that makes falling cost something even for a character who gains no power from it.

**Bearing:** What a person has become shows. A Dark-aligned character gains +1 to Intimidation at 25 and +2 at 75, and takes the same figure as a penalty to any reaction or social roll that depends on being trusted -- Diplomacy, Merchant when haggling in good faith, Savoir-Faire, and comparable attempts to be believed or welcomed. A Light-aligned character reverses it exactly: the bonus applies to trust-based rolls and the penalty to Intimidation. Neither side is better; each buys one kind of social leverage with the other. A character who conceals their alignment (Chapter 8's masking effects, a heavy hood, an unread reputation) may have the GM waive this for a scene.

**Droids:** Droids have Alignment and are subject to both effects above. A droid accumulates it the way anyone does -- through what it is ordered to do, what is done to it, and what it chooses when a gap opens in its orders -- and a droid that has spent decades killing is genuinely harder to restrain than one that has spent them repairing moisture vaporators. What droids do not have is a Force connection: none of the Force-specific modifiers below ever apply to them, and no amount of accumulated Darkness lets a droid touch the Force.
**The Force and Droid Minds:** A power fails against a droid, cyborg brain or artificial intelligence when it needs a mind to receive it, and works when it only needs senses or systems to fool.

**Mind-targeting powers fail outright, with no roll.** Influencing, dominating, terrifying or erasing a mind finds nothing to push against: Force Mind Trick (C1), Force Fear (C8), Mnemotherapy (C10), Qâzoi Kyantuska (E4) and Summon Fear (E6).
**Force Illusion (C9) works,** and says so in its own entry. It projects a false image rather than a suggestion, and a droid's optics can be fed a lie exactly as an eye can.

**Mechu-deru (E13) works, and is the sharper exception.** It does not persuade a droid at all but reaches into its systems directly -- a Force-borne intrusion closer to slicing than to suggestion, resolved as a Quick Contest against the droid's Will or HT.

**Its cost is deliberate.** That Mechu-deru is a Sith Alchemy power costing 25 CP to unlock reflects that reaching a machine mind through the Force is advanced, invasive work. The Jedi never developed a comparable technique.
**Three Ways to Reach a Droid, and They Do Not Overlap:** It is worth separating these, because all three get loosely described as “getting into a droid's head.”
**Suggestion powers simply fail.** They target an organic mind, and a droid has nothing to suggest to.

**Slicing is the ordinary route, and involves no Force at all.** Chapter 3, IQ/Very Hard: a mundane skill roll against the droid's own security, available to anyone, penalised -5 without gear. This is what Chapter 17's Digital Mind means by “susceptible to computer slicing.”
**Mechu-deru is the Force route.** It reaches the same systems by a different door -- a Quick Contest rather than a skill roll, no gear and no slicer needed.

**Field Detection is none of these.** A Miraluka's perception trait (Chapter 4) adds +3 to +5 to the mundane Slicing roll, so a Miraluka slicer is better at the ordinary route rather than having a fourth one. It never grants Force access to a droid, and it is never required to slice -- a character with the Slicing skill and a datapad needs nothing else.

Force-Sensitive Effects Only. The modifiers from here to the end of this section apply solely to characters who can touch the Force; a non-sensitive or a droid has an Alignment but none of these. Force Point Cost Modifier: A character's Force Alignment provides a discount to the FP cost of powers aligned with their current leaning. Characters whose alignment is equal to, or greater than 25 points on either the Light Side, Or Dark Side are considered aligned with that side.
The FP cost reduction for powers of the **same alignment** is 0.5% per point of alignment.
The FP cost reduction for **Neutral/Gray** powers is **0.5% × (25 − |Alignment|)**.

The FP cost penalty for powers of the **opposite alignment** is 0.5% per point of alignment. This is deliberate: full alignment buys the deepest discounts on your own side's powers and locks the other side out, while a grey Force-user keeps both sides open at only mild modifiers. Round any fractional Force Point cost, and any alignment- or Discord-scaled effect, to the nearest whole number.
**Applying the Discount/Penalty**

**Light Side Aligned Characters (Alignment +25 or higher):** Receive a discount on Light Side powers, no discount on Neutral/Gray powers, and a penalty on Dark Side powers. At maximum alignment (+100), this is a 50% discount for Light, full price for Neutral, and a 50% penalty for Dark.

**Dark Side Aligned Characters (Alignment -25 or lower):** Receive a discount on Dark Side powers, no discount on Neutral/Gray powers, and a penalty on Light Side powers. At maximum alignment (-100), this is a 50% discount for Dark, full price for Neutral, and a 50% penalty for Light.

**Neutral Characters (Alignment = 0):** A perfectly neutral character receives a **12.5% reduction** to Neutral power costs. As alignment shifts toward the edges of neutrality (±25), the reduction decreases gradually until it reaches **0%** at ±25. Once a character’s alignment passes beyond ±25 and they are considered **fully aligned** to either the Light or Dark side, this Neutral benefit ends.

sections.content: Once a character is officially aligned with one side of the Force (Alignment ≥ +25 for Light, ≤ −25 for Dark — see above), they can no longer learn **new** powers of the opposite alignment. Neutral powers remain learnable by anyone, regardless of alignment.

**This never strips away anything already known:** a Light-aligned character who learned a Dark power before crossing +25 keeps it — weakened by the Discord Penalty below — but the door to learning anything new from the opposing side closes the moment that threshold is crossed.

A character using a power that opposes their current alignment doesn’t just pay more for it (see the Force Point Cost Modifier above) — the power itself comes out weaker, the Force resisting a hand it doesn’t recognize.

At Alignment 0, this is ×1.0 — a true neutral has no opposing side, so nothing is discordant. At Alignment 100 (either direction), this is ×0.5 — half strength, the floor; opposition weakens a power but never fully cancels it out.
**Powers with a scaling numeric effect** (damage, range, duration, healing, bonus granted, etc.): multiply that number by your Discord Multiplier.

**Powers resolved by a roll or contest with no scaling number** (Force Mind Trick, Vanish, Force Illusion, and similar effects): subtract (1 − Discord Multiplier) × 20, rounded down, from that roll instead.
Force powers are categorized by their general effect and application.
Sense Powers allow the Force-user to perceive the environment or others beyond normal senses, providing crucial tactical information.

content: **Description:** Allows perception of the world through the Force, bypassing blindness, illusions, or even physical obstructions like smoke or darkness.
**Base Force Skill:** Sense (Per/Average)

**Description:** The Miralukan species is a force sensitive humanoid race born without eyes, who perceive the world through the Force. This aids them in bypassing blindness, illusions, or even physical obstructions like smoke, darkness, or physical objects.
**Base Force Skill:** Sense (Per/Average)
**Required Advantage:** Force Sight (Miraluka Specialized Vision)
**Description:** The Force-user can extend their senses beyond normal limits, perceiving events and locations at great distances through the Force, as if physically present.
**Base Force Skill:** Sense (Per/Average)
**Description:** The Force-user receives glimpses or warnings of future events, providing insight into impending danger, important developments, or potential outcomes.
**Base Force Skill:** Sense (Per/Average) or Observation (Per/Average)
**Description:** The Force-user can perceive echoes of the past by touching an object or entering a location where strong emotions or significant events have occurred.
**Base Force Skill:** Sense (Per/Average)
**Description:** The user masks their presence in the Force, making them difficult for other Force-sensitives to detect.
**Base Force Skill:** Stealth (DX/Average) or a contested Sense roll.
**Description:** The Force-user connects with the minds and emotions of non-sapient creatures, radiating peace to pacify aggressive beasts or forming a temporary alliance to gain their cooperation.
**Base Force Skill:** Animal Handling (IQ/Average) or Influence (Will/Hard).

sections.content: Control Powers allow the Force-user to directly manipulate objects, beings, or the environment through direct application of the Force.

content: **Description:** The Force-user can telekinetically push or pull objects and beings.
**Base Force Skill:** Telekinesis (Will/Hard)
**Description:** The Force-user enhances their physical jump or leap through an application of the Force.
**Base Force Skill:** Agility (DX/Hard)
**Description:** The Force-user accelerates their body and mind, allowing them to move and react with incredible swiftness.
**Base Force Skill:** Agility (DX/Hard)
**Description:** The Force-user creates a protective shield of pure energy to deflect or absorb incoming attacks.
**Base Force Skill:** Will
**Description:** The user channels their anger and pain into a terrifying surge of physical power, sacrificing defense for raw offensive capability.
**Base Force Skill:** Will

sections.content: **Description**: The Force-user telekinetically guides a thrown weapon, typically a lightsaber, allowing it to strike targets at a distance and return to their hand.

**Description**: A technique of extreme discipline, allowing the Jedi to transcend physical pain and trauma. They use the Force to suppress shock and agony so they can continue fighting to protect others. Effects last one minute per use.
**Description:** A Force wielder uses the Dark Side to telekinetically crush an opponent, or a specific part of them. You must be able to see the target.

**Resolution:** Roll a Quick Contest of your Force Skill vs. the target’s **HT** (to withstand the physical trauma) or **Will** (to telekinetically fight the grip). **If you win**, the target takes the damage listed in the table below.
**Margins of Victory: If you win by 3 or more**, you may choose a specific hit location (e.g., a limb, the neck, or the vitals). **If you win by 5 or more**, the damage is doubled.

**Simple Failure**: you lose your concentration and are mentally stunned for one turn (roll vs. IQ to recover) as the Force snaps back at you; you still pay the full FP cost, spent but unable to take hold.
**Critical Failure**: the Force backfires violently -- you take at least 1d crushing damage as the pressure reflects onto your own body, and are physically stunned for 1d turns.

**Description:** The Force-user forgoes physical grip entirely, animating and wielding one or more weapons purely through the Force. Attacks with a telekinetically-wielded weapon use the character’s Telekinesis skill in place of the weapon’s normal DX-based skill (e.g., Lightsaber Combat) for both to-hit and parry rolls. Each additional weapon controlled this way attacks independently on the user’s turn.

**Note:** The user’s own body has no physical grip on any weapon used this way, and gains no bonus to its own physical Parry from wielding one; a Master-tier user (see table below) can extend a telekinetic parry to their own body as well.
Alter Powers enable the Force-user to directly influence other beings’ minds, emotions, or to project destructive Force energy.

content: **Description:** The Force-user subtly influences the minds of others, planting suggestions, causing confusion, or altering perceptions. Resolved as a Quick Contest of the user's Influence against the target's Will. A target who is aware of the attempt, hostile, or asked to act against their own survival or a Code of Honor rolls at +5, and the GM may rule some suggestions simply impossible. This alters what a target believes; it does not alter what is physically there, which is Force Illusion (C9). Force Sight and Miralukan Force Sight let a user see through an illusion, but not through a suggestion -- a mind that has been persuaded has nothing false in front of it to see past.
**Base Force Skill:** Influence (Will/Hard)
**Description:** The Force-user generates raw electrical energy from their fingertips, unleashing potent bolts of Force lightning upon their foes.
**Base Force Skill:** Innate Attack (Energy) (DX/Easy)
**Description:** The Force-user can project a concentrated burst of Force energy that stuns or incapacitates a single target.
**Base Force Skill:** Will
**Description:** The Force-user conjures a devastating localized storm of Force energy, unleashing a torrent of destructive power upon an area.
**Base Force Skill:** Will
**Description:** An uncontrolled, raw release of Force energy triggered by extreme anger, pain, or frustration.
**Base Force Skill:** Will
**Description:** A potent Dark Side ability, this power allows the Force-user to siphon the life energy and Force potential of another being.
**Base Force Skill:** Will
**Description:** One of the most sinister Dark Side powers, Drain Life allows the user to violently rip a target’s life force away to mend their own body.
**Base Force Skill:** Will vs. HT (contested roll)
**Description:** The user projects a wave of terror into the minds of their enemies, causing them to flee or become paralyzed with fear.
**Base Force Skill:** Intimidation (Will/Average) or a contested Will roll.

**Description:** The user projects an image into the minds of beings in a radius to change the perception of what someone sees for the duration it is active, even electronic systems are not immune. User must concentrate, if hit, roll Will, illusion is broken on fail.
**Base Force Skill:** Influence (Will/Hard) vs target’s Perception.
**Description:** Visualizes a target’s memories and eradicates them.
**Base Force Skill:** Influence (Will/Hard) vs target’s Will.

**Description:** The user manipulates light & sound waves to become virtually invisible, and/ or unworthy of notice to others. While highly effective when practiced properly, maintaining such a cloak was extremely taxing and the concentration needed to make a convincing shroud could diminish the worth of employing the technique.
**Base Force Skill:** Influence (Will/Hard) vs target’s Perception.

**Description:** A strictly pacifistic combat technique. The user surrounds a target in a localized field of Force energy, temporarily paralyzing them and preventing them from causing harm without inflicting any physical injury.
**Base Force Skill:** Will vs. target’s HT (contested roll)
**Description:** The user channels the pure, luminous energy of the Light Side. This power purges dark side influence, blinding and severely weakening Dark Side users and their unnatural creations.
**Base Force Skill:** Will vs. target’s Will
**Description:** The Force-user channels life-giving energy through the Force to accelerate natural healing.
**Base Force Skill:** Healing (Will/Hard)
**Description:** A subtle but potent application of the Force, allowing the user to channel healing energies to mend fatigue and restore stamina.
**Base Force Skill:** Healing (Will/Hard)

sections.content: **Description**: The Force-user becomes a focal point of strategy and morale on the battlefield. By extending their senses and will through the Force, they can guide their allies with uncanny prescience while sowing seeds of doubt and confusion among their enemies. This is a concentration-based ability and its effects last as long as the user maintains it. The user is not able to use any other skills or powers during the time they are meditating.
**Base Force Skill:** Meditation (Will/Hard), Tactics (IQ/Hard) or Leadership (IQ/Average)

**Description**: The Force-user becomes a beacon of hope and resolve, radiating a luminous aura that bolsters the physical and mental fortitude of themselves and their allies, steeling them against the horrors of war.

Only characters who have fallen to Alignment –75 or deeper, and who possess the relevant unlocked power, are able to access and use these unnatural abilities. Rising back above –75 — even temporarily — immediately suspends access to every Sith Sorcery and Alchemy power the character knows. Nothing is lost permanently; the knowledge stays learned, but the Force itself refuses to answer until the character falls deep enough again.

Sith Sorcery and Alchemy abilities require an incantation per cast, which requires the user to be completely focused on the spell during that time, if the user is hit, or has to focus elsewhere, they must begin the casting again.

Some abilities must maintain concentration during use and will break the casting if interrupted while concentrating. If hit, or interrupted during either, roll 3d6, concentration kept on crit success. While concentrating, the user may take other actions that do not require use of the force.

**Unlocking a Power:** each Sith Sorcery or Alchemy power below lists its own CP Cost to unlock — a one-time investment representing the dangerous, unsupervised study it takes to reconstruct forbidden knowledge with no living teacher to guide you. There are no further tiers to purchase after that; once unlocked, a power is available at full strength any time the character's Alignment is –75 or deeper.

**Era Note:** This fits the setting at any point in the timeline (see the Timeline Guide, Chapter 21) -- these powers have never required a living Order to teach them. Before 3959 BBY, every practitioner is, by necessity, exactly this kind of self-taught cultist; after that date, some may instead have learned from an actual Sith Master.
**Corruption Multiplier:** the deeper into the Dark Side a character has fallen, the more powerful their Sorcery and Alchemy become.
At exactly –75, this is ×1.0 — the power works at its printed value. At −100 (total darkness), this is ×2.0. Each power below states exactly what its Corruption Scaling multiplies or modifies.

content: **Description:** Also known as “**Bolt of Hatred**”. The Force-user channels their hatred into a ball of dark energy and hurls it at an opponent up to 10 yards away, in their direct line of sight for 2d+3 damage.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 20 CP.
**Cost:** 5 FP per use.
**Incantation time:** 1 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the total rolled damage by your Corruption Multiplier.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** Also known as “**Force Net**”. While concentrating, the user summons a lattice of dark side energy to ensnare an opponent in an unbreakable web. Severs the ensnared’s connection to the force while bound, saps their strength (ST -1 per minute bound, recovered upon full rest), and can be tightened to slice the target (1d per second tightened).
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 20 CP.
**Cost:** 5 FP per cast, 3 FP per second concentrated.
**Incantation time:** 2 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the ST drain per minute bound, and the tightening damage (1d per second), by your Corruption Multiplier.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** The user conjures a black mist in a specific location within their line of sight, which sprouts terrible dark tendrils to strike/grab, burn, and/or completely disintegrate parts of an opponent they touch up to 1 meter away from the mist. Declare a location, a target, and a body part you wish to target. Deals 3d+3 damage, roll an additional 3d, on crit success, tendrils disintegrate the part of the opponent they made contact with.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 25 CP.
**Cost:** 7 FP per cast, 5 FP per sec concentrated.
**Incantation time:** 3 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the total rolled damage (including the additional 3d) by your Corruption Multiplier.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** Also known as “**Dominate Mind**”. The user targets someone within their line of sight and puts them into a hypnotic trance where the target is unable to move or speak, the caster is able to force them to end their life if they wish. Upon physical contact, the user gains complete control of the victims actions while under control of the caster. May be used on multiple victims at once (multiply the FP cost per individual affected).
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 40 CP.
**Cost:** 5 FP per cast.
**Incantation time:** None.
**Corruption Scaling:** add (Corruption Multiplier − 1) × 10, rounded down, to your Sith Sorcery skill for this contest.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard) vs Target’s Will

sections.content: E5. False Light Side Aura (Sorcery Power) [DS]

content: **Description:** Cloaks a Dark Side user’s aura with an aura of light using a complex spell that requires a delicate balance of focus, and strength.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 20 CP.
**Cost:** 5 FP per cast, 1 FP per sec concentrated.
**Incantation time:** 10 min.
**Corruption Scaling:** any Sense or Force-detection roll made against you while this is active suffers a penalty equal to (Corruption Multiplier − 1) × 10, rounded down.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** Caster forms complex hand signs and forces a target to experience their worst fears, to the point of hysteria. Victim must roll Will every 5 sec to keep from going comatose on fail, or completely mad and ending their own life, on crit fail. If the target survives, the spell’s effects last for 3d min after the caster has ended the spell and they no longer have to resist going comatose, or dying, but will still experience delusions brought by it.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 35 CP.
**Cost:** 5 FP per sec.
**Incantation time:** 5 sec.

**Corruption Scaling:** the target's Will roll suffers a penalty equal to (Corruption Multiplier − 1) × 10, rounded down, and the lingering duration (3d minutes) is multiplied by your Corruption Multiplier.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)
**Description:** Allows a caster to hide their presence in the force from one, or multiple individuals.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 15 CP.
**Cost:** 1 FP per sec.
**Incantation time:** 1 min.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the number of individuals you can conceal at once by your Corruption Multiplier (round down, minimum 1).
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** A highly advanced technique for transferring consciousness to another body, or object. In the case of another body, the caster rolls 3d6+Total FP vs the target’s 3d6 + Total FP, the highest number wins. If caster wins, target effectively dies, and the caster assumes the form of their target while keeping their own stats. Casters inventory is left on their old body and they gain access to the target’s inventory. Otherwise, if the target wins, the caster dies.

sections.content: In the case of an object, the caster rolls 3d6 and upon success, transfers into the object, effectively making the object sentient with their consciousness and maintaining their abilities. This can be treated like a conscious Sith Alchemy artifact (like a Sith Lord transferring consciousness into a holocron) and the user may transfer into another body again by performing the technique on a new target any time after a full rest.

content: **CP Cost (to unlock):** 60 CP.
**Cost:** 30 FP per cast.
**Incantation time:** 3 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** add (Corruption Multiplier − 1) × 10, rounded down, to your side of the contest roll.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** Also known as “**Reanimate Dead**”. The caster infuses fresh corpses with dark side energy, twisting them into mindless, aggressive thralls (Sith Undead) that obey the caster’s simple commands. The thralls possess the physical attributes (**ST**, **DX**, **HT**) of the original body but have no intelligence or skills, and feel no pain. They will fight until physically destroyed.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 30 CP.
**Cost:** 10 FP per corpse.
**Incantation time:** 5 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** the Sith Undead's ST, DX, and HT each gain a bonus equal to (Corruption Multiplier − 1) × 5, rounded down.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard)

**Description:** The core art of Sith flesh-crafting. The user channels pure dark side energy into a living creature over a long period, horribly mutating it into a dark side abomination (like a mutated massassi or rancor). The creature gains increased Strength and Health (+1d to **ST** and **HT**), unnatural armor (**DR** 4), and becomes highly aggressive and subservient to the dark side. On a critical failure during casting, the beast immediately frenzies and attacks the caster.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 30 CP.
**Cost:** 20 FP per cast.
**Incantation time:** 1 hour.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the +1d ST/HT bonus dice and the DR bonus by your Corruption Multiplier (round down).
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard) vs Target’s HT

**Description:** The caster alters a mundane liquid or gas into a potent, Force-infused toxin. When ingested, inhaled, or introduced to the bloodstream, the victim suffers 2d **toxic** damage and must immediately roll **Will**. On a failure, their connection to the Force is clouded (-4 to all **Force skills**) and they suffer debilitating dark side hallucinations for 1d hours.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 20 CP.
**Cost:** 8 FP per dose.
**Incantation time:** 10 min.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the toxic damage by your Corruption Multiplier, and the Force skill penalty increases from −4 to −4 × Corruption Multiplier (round down).
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard)

**Description:** Also known as “Summon Demon”. The caster summons a horrifying manifestation of dark side energy, often taking the form of a Smoke Demon. The entity can pass through small cracks, is highly resistant to physical damage (possessing physical intangibility against non-energy weapons), and strikes targets with pure dark side terror. It remains for 1 minute or until its HP is depleted.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 35 CP.
**Cost:** 15 FP per cast, 3 FP per minute concentrated to maintain.
**Incantation time:** 10 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the summoned entity's HP and the maintained duration by your Corruption Multiplier.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Sorcery (IQ/Hard)

**Description:** A dark side technique used to control, corrupt, and mutate mechanical and electronic systems. The caster can force a droid to obey their commands, overload a computer terminal, or twist a machine into a deadly trap. When used to subvert a droid or cyborg, the caster rolls a Quick Contest against the target’s **Will** or **HT** (whichever is higher).
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 25 CP.
**Cost:** 6 FP per cast, 2 FP per minute concentrated.
**Incantation time:** 2 sec.
**Corruption Scaling:** add (Corruption Multiplier − 1) × 10, rounded down, to your side of the Quick Contest.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard)

**Description:** The caster permanently infuses an object (like an amulet, armor piece/set, a weapon, etc) with dark side energy. The item becomes exceptionally durable (grants the item **DR** +10 and **HP** +20) and can grant the wearer a +1 to +3 bonus to a specific Force skill chosen at the time of creation. Because it requires tearing a piece of the caster’s dark essence, creating such an artifact permanently drains 1 point of maximum **FP** from the caster.
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 40 CP.
**Cost:** 50 FP per cast (plus 1 permanent FP).
**Incantation time:** 1d days.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the DR and HP bonuses by your Corruption Multiplier (round down), and the skill bonus cap increases from +3 to +3 × Corruption Multiplier (round down).
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard)

**Description:** The caster performs a chanted ritual using an altar to create and manipulate unnaturally hot, blue flames. The flames have a long range of 500 feet, and can be used to attack (Deals 3d burning to target on successful hit, or 2x 3d on critical success), or grab a target to draw them closer (Roll a Quick Contest of your **Force Skill** vs. target’s **Will** (to telekinetically fight the grip)).
**CP Cost (to unlock):** 25 CP.
**Cost:** 10 FP per cast, 3 FP per minute concentrated.
**Incantation time:** 1d minutes.
**Corruption Scaling:** multiply the total rolled damage by your Corruption Multiplier.
**Base Force Skill:** Sith Alchemy (IQ/Very Hard)
